accessNotes: clarity.design is a JS-rendered Angular app, so the documentation was read from its source in github.com/vmware-clarity/ng-clarity (projects/website/.../demos/charts). Colour tokens (--cds-alias-viz-*) were read from _alias-viz-colors.scss and theme.dark.scss and resolved to hex from the HSL values in _global-colors.scss (converted with Python colorsys, so hex may differ by ±1 from a browser's rounding). Clarity provides colour tokens and guidance only, not a chart library, so it says nothing concrete about gridline styles, font sizes in charts, legends placement etc.; the example images are schematic SVG illustrations.
summary: Enterprise product-UI design system (VMware/Broadcom) whose data-viz section is a token library plus accessibility guidance for dashboards that 'explain, explore, monitor'. Distinctive pieces: a 16-colour categorical palette ordered for contrast (blue, violet, dark aqua, lavender, pink, olive-lime...), theme-aware tokens with a full dark-mode set, severity colours for status/capacity charts, and mandatory 1px strokes (background-coloured between pie slices; --cds-alias-viz-border on sequential/diverging marks). Charts are rendered on Clarity's slate-grey 'construction' neutrals with Metropolis type.

colors.categoricalNotes: --cds-alias-viz-general-1..16. 'Primary Colors' 1-8, 'Additional Colors' 9-16. 'Colors are ordered from 1 to 16 for optimal contrast.' Limit to 8 colours for readability; never exceed 16 (group or rethink). Monochrome family variants also exist: -blue (#009adb, #00608a, #0079ad, #00364c), -violet (#9b32c8, #5d0085, #320047, #7c12a5), -aqua (#00565c, #003033, #00a2ad, #007780), -lime (#818f00, #373d00, #202400, #657000). Dark theme general-1..16: #2ec0ff, #ac50d3, #80f6ff, #6e72d8, #ea53ad, #c9dc18, #8b8dda, #00e4f5, #e7f471, #ce91e8, #34daa3, #c2dfff, #bb70db, #acf075, #ee77be, #66b0ff.
colors.notes: Sequential families (50..1000): blue (above), violet #faf0ff..#320047, ochre #fff9eb..#613900, aqua #ebfeff..#003033, green #eefce3..#1c3706, red #fff2f0..#701100; in light themes higher values are darker, in dark themes lighter colours represent larger values. Diverging palettes (identical in light and dark): violet-aqua (above, violet-700 -> neutral violet-50 #faf0ff -> aqua-900), blue-jade (#00608a..#66d1ff | #e5f7ff | #68e3ba..#006b47), blue-green (#00608a..#66d1ff | #e5f7ff | #86e935..#366a0c), green-yellow-red (#42810e..#acf075 | #ffe875 | #ff816b..#8f1500). Severity: neutral #4f6169, success #42810e, warning #bd7e00, warning-light #ffc60a (light theme only with a 1px inner border in warning colour; never for labels/icons/lines), immediate #ff8e3d, critical #e02200, free-space fill #e3eaed + border #859399 (always together). Dark-theme severity: neutral #aeb8bc, success #67ca16, warning #ffda24, immediate #ff8e3d, critical #e02200, free-space fill #2d4048. --cds-alias-viz-border: #17252b light / #f3f5f7 dark. Dark app background construction-1000 #1b2b32, containers #21333b. Axis colour #4f6169 is the severity-neutral/construction-600 token, matched to the schematic illustrations (sampled #495a67); text colours are Clarity typography tokens color-400/300.

axisTitle.placement: label both axes with units of measurement

typography.notes: Chart guidance only says 'Use clear, readable fonts'. Clarity typography tokens: font-family 'Metropolis', 'Avenir Next', sans-serif; font sizes 10/11/12... (x scale); weights 300/400/500/600 (bold = 600); body letter-spacing -0.00714286em.

structure.gridlines: 'Avoid clutter by using only necessary gridlines.' Illustrations show none.
structure.axisLine: Illustrations show solid dark slate L-shaped x and y axis lines (~3px at illustration scale) with rounded caps.
structure.zeroLine: Diverging: ensure the midpoint (zero or average) is clearly defined.
structure.yAxisTitle: Label both axes clearly with units of measurement
structure.background: light theme white; dark theme #1b2b32 app / #21333b container
structure.notes: Position a data table near the chart for precise reference.

legend.placement: visible but not obstructing the chart (unspecified side)
legend.directLabels: Add direct labels to bars, lines and segments; use callouts or annotations for key points.
legend.notes: Interactive legends that highlight the corresponding data are recommended.

marks.bars: 1px stroke using --cds-alias-viz-border at the end of each bar/segment that uses sequential or diverging palettes.
marks.lines: Illustrations: medium solid lines with distinct marker shapes per series (circle, triangle) for dual encoding.
marks.points: Use different shapes plus colour (dual encoding).
marks.pies: 1px stroke between slices matching the background (white light theme, dark in dark theme).
marks.notes: Heatmaps: 1px --cds-alias-viz-border stroke on cells using sequential/diverging palettes.

labels.dataLabels: Direct labels on bars, lines and segments to reduce reliance on colour.

furniture.title: Concise, descriptive title that communicates the main topic or insight.
furniture.other: Offer data as a table near the chart or as a downloadable file.

annotations: Use callouts or annotations to highlight key data points.
interaction: Tooltips on hover with exact values, categories or dates; sufficient contrast; not overloaded. Illustration shows a white tooltip with a 2px blue (#009adb) border, small pointer tail at bottom-left, dark slate text, rounded corners; hovered point shown as a hollow circle marker. Interactive legends highlight corresponding data.
accessibility: Patterns and textures with dual encoding (colour + pattern); high-contrast colours; avoid red-green and blue-purple pairs; avoid information overload; clear labels; alternative formats (table, download); test with Coblis or Stark. Severity warning-light fails contrast and requires a 1px inner border of the warning colour. Free-space fill must always be paired with its border.

distinctiveRules.rule: Categorical colours come in a fixed 1-16 order optimised for contrast, starting #009adb blue, #7c12a5 violet, #00565c dark aqua, #6e72d8 lavender, #d23292 pink, #818f00 olive, #2429c2 indigo, #00a2ad aqua.
distinctiveRules.quote: Colors are ordered from 1 to 16 for optimal contrast.

distinctiveRules.rule: Use at most 8 categorical colours; never more than 16.
distinctiveRules.quote: Limit colors to 8 for optimal readability ... Avoid exceeding 16 colors

distinctiveRules.rule: Pie slices and other clustered colours are separated by a 1px stroke in the background colour (white in light, dark in dark theme).
distinctiveRules.quote: Utilize 1 px stroke in pie charts ... Stroke color should match the background

distinctiveRules.rule: Bars, heatmap cells and segments using sequential/diverging colours get a 1px border in --cds-alias-viz-border (#17252b light, #f3f5f7 dark).
distinctiveRules.quote: Utilize 1 px stroke and use --cds-alias-viz-border for the border color at the end of each bar, heatmap, segment

distinctiveRules.rule: Sequential scales invert with theme: darker = higher in light theme, lighter = higher in dark theme; diverging palettes are unchanged across themes.
distinctiveRules.quote: In light themes, higher values are associated with darker colors. In dark themes, the lighter colors represent larger values.

distinctiveRules.rule: Status charts use only the severity set: neutral grey #4f6169, success green #42810e, warning #bd7e00, immediate orange #ff8e3d, critical red #e02200.
distinctiveRules.quote: Stick to a strict set of status colors (gray, green, yellow, orange, red)

distinctiveRules.rule: Capacity charts show free space as #e3eaed fill always with a #859399 border.
Bright warning-light yellow #ffc60a must carry a 1px inner border in warning #bd7e00 and is never used for labels, icons or lines.
distinctiveRules.quote: must always be used alongside an inner border ... Never use Severity Warning-Light ... for labels, icons and line charts

distinctiveRules.rule: Dual encoding: pair colour with patterns/textures or marker shapes; avoid red-green and blue-purple pairs.
distinctiveRules.quote: Use both color and pattern to encode information.

distinctiveRules.rule: Full dark-mode palette: categorical colours shift to lighter tints (#2ec0ff, #ac50d3, #80f6ff, ...) on #1b2b32/#21333b backgrounds.
Tooltips show exact values/categories/dates with sufficient contrast; legends are interactive and highlight the matching series.
distinctiveRules.quote: Include relevant details such as exact values, categories, or dates.

distinctiveRules.rule: Use only necessary gridlines; label both axes with units.
distinctiveRules.quote: Label both axes clearly with units of measurement ... using only necessary gridlines

distinctiveRules.rule: Provide the chart's data as a table near the chart or as a download.
distinctiveRules.quote: Position the table near the chart for easy comparison.

referenceImages.describes: Schematic line chart: thick dark-slate (#495a67) L-shaped y and x axis lines with rounded caps, no ticks, labels, gridlines or title. Two straight-segment lines: violet (#7c12a5, general-2) with filled triangle markers and blue (#009adb, general-1) with filled circle markers — dual encoding by shape. White background.

Schematic grouped column chart: two groups of three square-cornered columns in categorical order blue #009adb, violet #7c12a5, dark aqua #00565c, small gaps between columns and a larger gap between groups; dark-slate axis lines, no gridlines or labels.

Tooltip anatomy: two lines in dark slate and light grey with hollow white-filled circle markers outlined in the line colour; a hand cursor hovers a point; tooltip is a white rounded rectangle with a 2px blue #009adb border and a small pointer tail at bottom-left, containing dark slate (#22343c) sans text 'This is a tooltip'.
